extracted.subtask_description: Guidance on claiming and perfecting foreign priority/benefit, and on adding inadvertently omitted specification/drawing material by incorporation under 37 CFR 1.57(a), including examiner procedures and required filings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Director's authority to accept unintentionally delayed foreign priority claims
rubrics_metrics.description: The Director may consider failure to file a timely claim for priority as a waiver, but may establish procedures (including a surcharge) to accept an unintentionally delayed claim.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Director may require a certified copy of the original foreign application, specification, and drawings upon which it is based, a translation if not in English, and any other information deemed necessary. Certification must be by the foreign intellectual property authority and show application and filing dates. Acceptance procedures may include payment of a surcharge.

rubrics_metrics.name: Post-issuance cure of failure to perfect foreign priority benefits
rubrics_metrics.description: A failure to perfect a claim to foreign priority benefit prior to issuance may be cured by filing a reissue application or, under certain conditions, by requesting a certificate of correction under 35 U.S.C. 255 and 37 CFR 1.323.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Certificate of correction may be used where the parent application satisfied 35 U.S.C. 119(a)-(d) or (f) prior to issuance and the continuing application essentially affirms the previously expressed desire to receive benefits (e.g., In re Van Esdonk). If statutory requirements were not met in the patented application or its parent prior to issuance, certificate of correction cannot perfect the claim — reissue is required (see Brenner v. State of Israel).

rubrics_metrics.name: Post-issuance correction and petition requirements for certain 111(a) applications
rubrics_metrics.description: If the original application that issued as the patent was filed under 35 U.S.C. 111(a) (other than a design application) on or after November 29, 2000, a priority claim under 35 U.S.C. 119(a)-(d) or (f) may be added or corrected in the issued patent by reissue or certificate of correction, assuming conditions for reissue/certificate are otherwise met.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In addition to filing reissue or certificate of correction, the patentee must file a petition to accept a delayed claim for priority under 35 U.S.C. 119(a)-(d) or (f) with the surcharge set forth in 37 CFR 1.17(t) and a statement that the entire delay between the due date under 37 CFR 1.55(a)(1) and filing was unintentional (see 37 CFR 1.55(c)).

rubrics_metrics.name: General rule for incorporation by reference under 37 CFR 1.57(a)
rubrics_metrics.description: If all or a portion of the specification or drawings is inadvertently omitted from an application, but the application contains a claim under 37 CFR 1.55 (foreign priority) or 37 CFR 1.78 (benefit of prior-filed provisional/nonprovisional/international application) that was present on the filing date, and the omitted portion is completely contained in the prior-filed application, the claim shall be considered an incorporation by reference of the prior-filed application as to the omitted portion.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This provides a safeguard for applicants when material was inadvertently omitted (e.g., clerical error) and allows that material to be added later by amendment if other requirements are met. See also explicit incorporation guidance in MPEP § 608.01(p).

rubrics_metrics.name: Conditions and requirements for adding omitted material under 37 CFR 1.57(a)
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicants must satisfy a set of conditions (A)–(I) for 37 CFR 1.57(a) to apply.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The requirements are: (A) application filed on or after Sept 21, 2004; (B) material was inadvertently omitted; (C) claim under 37 CFR 1.55 or 1.78 present on filing date; (D) omitted portion is completely contained in the prior-filed application; (E) applicant must amend to include omitted portion within any time set by Office but no later than close of prosecution (37 CFR 1.114(b)) or abandonment; (F) if not otherwise entitled to a filing date, amendment must be by petition under 37 CFR 1.57(a) with fee in 1.17(f); (G) supply a copy of the prior-filed application (except where prior-filed app was filed under 35 U.S.C. 111); (H) supply English translation of any non-English prior-filed application; (I) identify where the omitted portion is found in the prior-filed application.

rubrics_metrics.name: No formal declaration required for inadvertence; certification effect
rubrics_metrics.description: There is no requirement to submit a separate declaration proving the omission was inadvertent at the time of filing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Submitting an amendment under 37 CFR 1.57(a) constitutes a certification under 37 CFR 10.18(b) that the omission was inadvertent. The Office may inquire about inadvertence if the record raises such issue.

rubrics_metrics.name: Priority/benefit claim must be present on filing date
rubrics_metrics.description: For incorporation by reference under 37 CFR 1.57(a), the priority claim under 1.55 or benefit claim under 1.78 of the prior-filed application must have been present on the filing date of the later-filed application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The later-filed application claiming benefit can be a continuation, divisional, or continuation-in-part. Presence on filing date is a strict requirement for 1.57(a) incorporation relief.

rubrics_metrics.name: "Completely contained" requirement for omitted material
rubrics_metrics.description: Material to be added under 37 CFR 1.57(a) must be 'completely contained' in the prior-filed application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: 'Completely contained' means the material must be expressly (not implicitly) disclosed in the prior-filed application, and must be contained in the prior application as filed (i.e., as originally filed).

rubrics_metrics.name: Timing and manner of amendment to add inadvertently omitted material
rubrics_metrics.description: Amendment to include omitted material must be filed within any time period set by the Office, but in no case later than close of prosecution as defined in 37 CFR 1.114(b), or abandonment, whichever occurs earlier.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If OIPE mails a Notice of Omitted Item(s) giving a two-month reply period, the amendment should be submitted within that two-month period and identified as an amendment under 37 CFR 1.57(a). An amendment submitted in reply to a final Office action does not have a right of entry (it will be treated under 37 CFR 1.116). If prosecution is closed, applicant may file an RCE (37 CFR 1.114) or petition to revive (37 CFR 1.137) as appropriate. 37 CFR 1.57(a) cannot be used to add omitted material to an already issued patent (certificate of correction or reissue would be required).

rubrics_metrics.name: Petition requirement when application not entitled to a filing date
rubrics_metrics.description: If the application is not otherwise entitled to a filing date under 37 CFR 1.53(b), the amendment to add omitted material must be made by petition under 37 CFR 1.57(a) with the petition fee under 37 CFR 1.17(f).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If OIPE mails a 'Notice of Incomplete Application' indicating lack of specification or drawings, applicant should file a petition under 37 CFR 1.57(a) in response to rely on 1.57(a). See MPEP § 601.01(d) and (f).

rubrics_metrics.name: Effect on international applications
rubrics_metrics.description: Any amendment to an international application under 37 CFR 1.57(a) is effective only as to the United States and has no effect on the international filing date.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Incorporation by reference relief in 1.57(a) cannot be relied upon to accord or alter an international filing date under PCT Article 11. No request to add omitted material in an international application designating the U.S. will be acted on before entry and commencement of national stage (37 CFR 1.491) or filing under 35 U.S.C. 111(a) claiming benefit.

rubrics_metrics.name: Examples illustrating application of 37 CFR 1.57(a)
rubrics_metrics.description: Practical examples show how Figure omission, last-page omission after prosecution closed, and multi-application chains are treated under 1.57(a).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example 1: OIPE notices omitted Figure 3; applicant must amend within two months in compliance with 1.57(a). Example 2: Last page omitted after prosecution closed — applicant must reopen prosecution via RCE and file amendment in compliance with 1.57(a) before paying issue fee unless petition to withdraw from issue filed. Example 3: In chain of applications where an intermediate application is abandoned, applicant may need to amend both the intermediate and later applications and file a petition to revive the intermediate solely to correct the specification under 1.57(a).

rubrics_metrics.name: Form paragraph 6.19.02 to notify noncompliance with 37 CFR 1.57(a)
rubrics_metrics.description: Examiners may use form paragraph 6.19.02 to notify applicants that an amendment to add inadvertently omitted material pursuant to 37 CFR 1.57(a) is not in compliance, and must state the reason(s).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Bracket 1 inserts date of amendment; Bracket 2 inserts reason(s) such as (1) application filed before Sept 21, 2004; (2) claim for priority/benefit not present on filing date; (3) omitted portion not completely contained in prior-filed application; (4) copy of prior-filed application not submitted (except 35 U.S.C.111 cases); (5) English translation not submitted; (6) location of omitted portion not identified. If amendment introduces new matter, follow with form paragraph 7.28; if it adds or affects claims, also follow with form paragraph 7.31.01. After-final amendments raising new issues should receive an advisory action.

rubrics_metrics.name: Examiner responsibility to verify prior-application data (cross-noting)
rubrics_metrics.description: Examiners should review the identifying data of all prior applications for which benefits are claimed to ensure accuracy and that the data is provided in the specification or application data sheet (see 37 CFR 1.78(a) and MPEP § 201.11).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Front page of printed patent identifies prior applications for which benefits are claimed. Where prior application data is preprinted on PALM bib-data sheet, the examiner should check that data for accuracy and initial the PALM bib-data sheet in the provided space when correct. Corrections to preprinted data can be made by Technology Center technical support staff, and a new sheet printed and scanned into the file. Inclusion of prior application information on the patent front page does not necessarily indicate claims are entitled to the earlier filing date.

rubrics_metrics.name: Notation on file wrapper when foreign priority is claimed
rubrics_metrics.description: PALM bib-data sheet should include application number, country (or IP authority), and day/month/year of each foreign application claimed for priority; examiner should check accuracy and correct as needed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If certified copies of each foreign application have been received, information for each foreign application should be entered on the PALM bib-data sheet. The front page and Official Gazette listing will refer to the claim of priority (country, filing date, number) for those where the PALM bib-data sheet is endorsed. Examiner must indicate on Office action and PALM bib-data sheet whether the conditions of 35 U.S.C. 119(a)-(d) or (f) have been met. For provisional benefits claimed under 35 U.S.C.119(e), do not reflect earlier applications to which the provisional claims priority.

rubrics_metrics.name: Oath or declaration requirement to identify foreign applications
rubrics_metrics.description: 37 CFR 1.63 requires that the oath or declaration must identify any foreign application for which a claim for priority is made pursuant to 37 CFR 1.55, and any foreign application having a filing date before that of the application on which priority is claimed, by specifying application number, country, day, month, and year of filing (unless supplied on an application data sheet under 37 CFR 1.76).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examiner should ensure the oath/declaration or application data sheet contains the required identifying information for claimed foreign priorities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definitions of application status categories
rubrics_metrics.description: The MPEP defines statuses used to classify applications: new, rejected, amended, allowed/in issue, abandoned, incomplete.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: 'New' = nonprovisional not yet received examiner action; 'Rejected' = contains an unanswered examiner's action before allowance; 'Amended' = applicant has replied to examiner's action; 'Allowed/in issue' = examined and passed to issue subject to payment of issue fee; 'Abandoned' = removed from Office docket (see enumerated causes); 'Incomplete' = not entitled to a filing date (lacking essential parts). Examiners should apply these definitions when logging and processing files.

rubrics_metrics.name: Status inquiry timing and applicant guidance
rubrics_metrics.description: Guidance on when applicants should inquire about application status for new and amended applications.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: New applications: status inquiry appropriate if Notice of Allowance not received within three months from receipt of form PTOL-37. Amended applications: examiner expected to act within two months of receiving amendment; applicants should not inquire until 5-6 months have elapsed without response; if six months elapse with no reply, applicant should inquire to avoid abandonment. Applicants are encouraged to use PAIR to check status. A stamped postcard receipt for replies to Office actions, adequately identifying papers filed, is prima facie proof of receipt and can obviate petition to revive if timely.

rubrics_metrics.name: Processing status letters by Technology Centers (TCs)
rubrics_metrics.description: TCs must follow specified steps when processing status letters and inquiries.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Steps include (A) deliver status letters to designated TC location; (B) designated representative reviews nature of request and entitlement (use PALM Intranet); (C) determine appropriate reply by using PALM Intranet, reviewing dates/tracking, discussing with supervisory examiners, or reviewing application file; (D) may reply by phone or written fax/mail; (E) note reply on status letter with initials/date; (F) employ Status Letter Database to track progress and retain records; (G) associate the status letter and reply with the application file (including abandoned apps). For PCT applications, forward to PCT Legal Division. For patented applications, forward to File Information Unit.

rubrics_metrics.name: Handling Congressional and other official inquiries
rubrics_metrics.description: Correspondence and inquiries from the White House, Members of Congress, embassies, and heads of Executive departments/agencies should be cleared through the Office of International Relations and/or Office of Congressional Relations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Such requests should be referred initially to a staff member in the appropriate office to ensure uniform handling and compliance with Department of Commerce directives.
